subject: Successful inla.cpo results still include failures

messages.author: a96aa45411c16ae6
messages.subject: Successful inla.cpo results still include failures
parts:
Dear R-INLA Community:

Hello,
I am fitting spatiotemporal hierarchical models with spatial, temporal, and spatiotemporal interaction terms and a random slope for one of covariates. Since my model fit results had 198 failures for CPO computation, I ran inla.cpo.

> model_cpo_fixed <- inla.cpo(model_original, mc.cores=1)

After 12+ hours, the function prompted that CPOs were fixed. However, the new object for inla.cpo results still include 197 failures.

> summary(model_cpo_fixed$cpo$failure)
    Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max.
0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.006657 0.000000 1.000000
> summary(model_original$cpo$failure)
    Min.  1st Qu.   Median     Mean  3rd Qu.     Max.
0.000000 0.000000 0.000000 0.006724 0.000000 1.000000

Did I do something wrong? I looked into inla.cpo source code (https://github.com/hrue/r-inla/blob/devel/rinla/R/cpo.R) and it is supposed to return a result with no CPO failures.

Any advice will be very much appreciated.
Thank you.
Best,
Insang Song

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Successful inla.cpo results still include failures
parts:
Try this, which uses a new implementation of the cpo

library(INLA)
data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
Germany$id <- 1:nrow(Germany)
formula3 = Y ~ f(region, model="besag", graph=g) + f(id) + f(x,
model="rw2")

## just to get 'cpo' for comparison
r = inla(formula3, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E,
control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE))
cpo <- r$cpo$cpo


r = inla(formula3, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E)
r <- inla.group.cv(r)

plot(cpo, r$cv, log = "xy", pty = 19)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lwd = 3)
